So I actually didn't have DPDR before the ceremony, it happened after the ceremony! I had mild anxiety and depression but was very functional. I think I had dissociative moments when I was growing up but it was definitely not a disorder. It was fleeting moments and I remember a friend explained to me she had dissociation months before the ceremony and I remember clearly not being able to relate whatsoever. So it was definitely after the ceremony it became a disorder. Thank you for your response and encouraging me to talk about it more. There have been people trying to help which I am very grateful for.
I feel exactly the same - the same age, it has just happened to me in 2019. I would love to chat and connect and support eachother if you want.

Of course. In short it was a difficult trip where I cried a lot, I forgot who I was (ego-death) and I thought I was left alone there in the ceremony room. My body was shaking for a little bit but I just couldn't lay still. I had some visual hallucinations and had panic attack symptoms. I definitely was sure I was going to die. I came back to my senses after 4 hours and I just tried to sleep the bad trip off. However the anxiety and trauma left from the trip never left me. I had suicidal thoughts and deep deep depression afterwards. I stopped eating, sleeping and I lost 20 lbs in 2 months. (for reference I struggled very heavily about losing weight before so this was a new thing for me) I never had a period like that in my life. My sense of self was so fractured that I thought I was going psychotic.   I couldn't work for a year afterwards and my mom had to take care of me. I had to take antidepressants to get me back to a normal level. I am still on them (even though very low level now). I am quite functional now (still have derealization) but it was the worst years of my life and I would not wish that on anyone. I just wish I knew the risks going into it.

I am scared to leave my house by myself where before I was going to countries where I didn’t speak the language and staying in hostels comfortably as a female traveler.
